title: a new compatibility shim, by its words

explain.what: A comment or a string uses words that describe keeping an old form alive: old name, still accepted, falls back to, for old links.
explain.why: A compatibility shim keeps old behaviour working after a rename. It is tech debt: two ways stay alive, and nobody knows when the old one may go (CLAUDE.md, No compatibility shims).
explain.fix: Change every caller, link, test and doc to the new form, and delete the old one. If the words describe something else, reword them.

patterns: \b(?:[Oo]ld names?|keeps? resolving|still accepted|for old links|folds? into|falls? back to)\b

head.src/b.py:
# the old name keeps resolving for old links
MSG = 'the --tab flag is still accepted'
head.src/c.rs:
// the old name keeps resolving for old links
pub const MSG: &str = "the --tab flag is still accepted";
head.src/d.ts:
// the old name keeps resolving for old links
export const MSG: string = 'the --tab flag is still accepted';

head.web/third_party/lib/x.mjs:
// the old name keeps resolving: falls back to the new one
export const a = 1;
head.crates/core/src/env_tests.rs:
// falls back to the old name when the new one is gone
pub const A: u8 = 1;
head.games/g/tests/test_a.py:
# falls back to the old name when the new one is gone
A = 1
head.pkg/test_b.py:
# falls back to the old name when the new one is gone
B = 1
head.src/b.py:
# a rename changes every caller
old_name = 1
# "falls back to" is a phrase this rule reads
head.src/d.ts:
// a rename changes every caller
export const oldName: number = 1;
